stem:
Girish plans to spot Venus from his roof at 7:30 p.m. Venus is above the horizon, but thick cloud covers the whole sky and nearby street lamps stay on.

Which judgment about seeing Venus that evening is correct?

options.text: He will see Venus clearly: it is above the horizon at that clock time.
He is unlikely to see Venus: clouds and bright lights block a clear dark view.
Switching on more roof lights will make Venus easier to find against the clouds.
Venus can be seen from every place on Earth at 7:30 p.m., so cloud cover does not matter.

teacher.key_rationale: Horizon time is not enough. Clear dark sky is also needed.
